profile.headline: Backend and AI engineer building
profile.intro: Async FastAPI backends, vector search, and cloud-integrated data pipelines — designed for concurrency, then measured against real numbers.

projects.name: Career Guidance AI
projects.stack: FastAPI · SQLAlchemy · pgvector · ONNX MiniLM · Caddy · React
points: Deterministic parse: pdfplumber with a pdfminer and pdftotext fallback, plus OCR only when a page is scanned — zero model calls in the parse path.
A confidence score gates everything downstream: 0.75 and above is accepted, 0.50 to 0.75 goes to human review, below that fails before any embedding or matching runs.
28,016-line backend, 73 routes, 32 tables, 304 tests — a three-tier embedding cache keyed by payload hash, and eager loading that removed the ranking loop N+1.

projects.name: Insurance Policy Document Handler
points: Versioned document store keyed by vehicle registration: upload assigns max+1, flips the previous row to superseded, and enforces uniqueness on (registration, type, version).

S3 writes fan out concurrently inside the same database transaction, so a failure mid-upload rolls back every row while objects already written stay in the bucket — the trade-off is documented rather than hidden.
Reads are presigned for one hour instead of proxied, failing per document; a five-year retention window is anchored to policy expiry and purged only by an explicit, dry-run-first admin action.

projects.name: JiraSync
points: Replaces a fragile Appfire OData connector with a Postgres warehouse Power BI reads directly, using JSONB expression indexes so project and priority slicers do not scan.
Two cadences: a 15-minute watermark sync that cannot see deletions, and a nightly full ID-set diff that exists only to catch them — plus advisory locks that make an overlapping run a silent skip.
Jira client pacing of 100 ms per call with five attempts, exponential backoff at 2.5x and Retry-After honoured; schema drift against field_map alerts to Slack.

projects.name: YourPDF
projects.stack: Next.js · FastAPI · pypdf · Ghostscript · Tesseract · Docker · Cloud Run
points: Twenty-eight PDF, image and office tools behind one API — every job returns inside the request that started it, with no queue, no worker and no polling.
Four external binaries do the work (Ghostscript, LibreOffice, OCRmyPDF with Tesseract, poppler) against temp files under /app/tmp that are removed in a finally block.
Files are processed server-side and deleted after the response; no accounts, no trackers, no stored output, and password operations never touch disk.
